# `Q-23-4` — References Div Outside The References Chapter

> A book chapter has a `#refs` div, but a book has one bibliography
> and it goes into another chapter. This div stays empty.

## What this means

An HTML book has one bibliography for the whole book, written into one
references chapter. A `#refs` div in any other chapter is not filled:
it renders as an empty div. A single document works differently. There,
a `#refs` div marks where that document's own reference list goes.

## Why this happens

The references chapter is the chapter `book.references` names. If that
key is not set, it is the first chapter, in book order, that contains a
`#refs` div. This warning appears on every other chapter that also has
a `#refs` div.

## How to fix

Remove the `#refs` div from the chapter the warning names. If that
chapter is the one that should hold the bibliography, name it with
`book.references` in `_quarto.yml`, or remove the `#refs` div from the
chapters before it.

## Related
